resharper_csharp_wrap_verbatim_interpolated_strings #

Arrangement of interpolated strings — Wrap interpolated strings. ⚠ Honoured by the oracle at the export's own settings, and read by no spelling in Skala. Measured on constructs/wrapping/interpolated-strings.cs, whose strings overflow at 120 columns: the three values produce three distinct oracle outputs — no_wrap leaves the string whole, wrap_if_long breaks inside the first interpolation hole, chop_if_long puts every hole's expression on a line of its own. All three spellings the export may write (resharper_, resharper_csharp_ and bare) reach the same behaviour, so this is one of the unprefixed forms the C# formatter does read. ⚠ The oracle glob is deliberately still null: Skala reads none of them, so the sweep can only report INERT — measured, with the glob set on this fixture for one run: oracle 3 distinct outputs, Skala 1, agreement at 1 of 3 values (the export's own, so the baseline agrees), verdict INERT — and SkalaSideTests.EverySweptOption_MovesSkalasOutputOnItsOwnFixture would go red. The fixture is committed and byte-exact at the export's value — point the glob at it when the key is implemented.

Typeone of wrap_if_long, chop_if_long, no_wrap
Defaultno_wrap
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two
